Architecture Diagram

The application is a single ASP.NET Web Forms site for browsing and maintaining a product catalog. It runs with in-memory mock catalog data by default, with an Entity Framework and SQL Server LocalDB path available when mock mode is disabled.

Data Storage & External Services

The configured database is SQL Server LocalDB. UseMockData defaults to true, so the default runtime path uses a shared in-memory catalog; setting it to false activates Entity Framework persistence. Application Insights is the only identified external telemetry integration; no external business APIs or message brokers were found.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac registers the catalog service per request for database mode and as a singleton in mock mode.
  • Entity Framework 6 maps catalog items, brands, and types to SQL Server tables.
  • ASP.NET Web Forms handles both page rendering and catalog form submissions.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports maintaining and browsing an e-commerce product catalog. Users can inspect catalog items and create, edit, or delete products; brands and types classify the catalog items.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemeShopLegacyWebForms / CatalogProduct offered in the catalog, with price, stock, and image informationEach item belongs to one brand and one type
CatalogBrandeShopLegacyWebForms / CatalogBrand classification for productsA brand can classify many catalog items
CatalogTypeeShopLegacyWebForms / CatalogType or category classification for productsA type can classify many catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopLegacyWebFormsProduct CatalogCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server LocalDB when mock mode is disabled; otherwise an in-memory mock

All catalog behavior belongs to one application; no cross-service ownership or event exchange was identified.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse Catalog

  1. A visitor opens the home page or a paginated catalog route.
  2. The page resolves the requested page size and index and calls ICatalogService.
  3. The service returns catalog items ordered by ID, together with brand and type data.
  4. The page renders the item list and navigation summary.
  5. In default mock mode, data comes from the singleton in-memory mock; database mode uses EF6.

Workflow 2: Create Catalog Item

  1. A user opens the create page and submits catalog fields.
  2. The page checks ModelState; invalid input does not proceed to persistence.
  3. The page constructs a CatalogItem from the form values and resolves brand and type selections.
  4. The catalog service assigns an ID and adds the item to the mock collection or EF context; database mode saves changes.
  5. The user is redirected to the catalog listing.

Workflow 3: Edit or Delete Catalog Item

  1. The page resolves the item ID from the route and loads the item through the catalog service.
  2. For editing, the page creates an updated item from submitted form values and asks the service to update it.
  3. For deletion, the page passes the loaded item to the service for removal.
  4. Database mode persists each operation through EF6 SaveChanges; mock mode mutates the shared in-memory list.
  5. The user is redirected to the catalog listing.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No cross-service calls, message brokers, or gateway aggregation were found. Catalog items, brands, and types are composed within the same application through the catalog service; the database-backed service loads brand and type navigation data through EF6.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Visitor participant Page as "Catalog page" participant Service as "Catalog service" participant Context as "EF6 DbContext" participant Database as "SQL Server LocalDB" participant Mock as "In-memory catalog" Visitor->>Page: Browse catalog Page->>Service: Request items and page alt Mock data enabled Service->>Mock: Read shared catalog list Mock-->>Service: Items with brand and type else Database mode Service->>Context: Query ordered catalog items Context->>Database: Read items and lookup entities Database-->>Context: Catalog records Context-->>Service: Items with brand and type end Service-->>Page: Paginated catalog Page-->>Visitor: Render item list Visitor->>Page: Submit create or edit form Page->>Page: Check ModelState alt Valid form Page->>Service: Create or update item alt Mock data enabled Service->>Mock: Mutate in-memory catalog Mock-->>Service: Operation complete else Database mode Service->>Context: Save changes Context->>Database: Persist catalog item Database-->>Context: Save result end Service-->>Page: Operation complete Page-->>Visitor: Redirect to catalog else Invalid form Page-->>Visitor: Render validation errors end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • CatalogItem price is constrained to non-negative values with at most two decimal places; stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock values are range-constrained by model annotations.
  • Catalog items require a valid brand and type relationship in the EF6 model.
  • The service assigns IDs using a SQL HiLo sequence in database mode and increments the maximum ID in mock mode.
  • Create and edit handlers proceed only when ModelState.IsValid; the delete handler removes the loaded item.
  • Persistence operations are saved through EF6 SaveChanges; no distributed transaction, saga, or explicit audit trail was found.
  • The application has no identified role-based authorization checks for catalog mutation workflows.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and relies on older System.Web, EF6, and package versions. The dependency scan found medium-or-higher advisories affecting Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1 and log4net 2.0.10; see the security assessment for the advisory details. The legacy project format and Web Forms packages constrain migration to modern .NET.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The data model is a product catalog with three Entity Framework 6 entities stored in SQL Server LocalDB when database mode is selected. The default configuration enables mock data, so the normal startup path uses an in-memory catalog instead.

Entity definitions are in src/eShopLegacyWebForms/Models/CatalogItem.cs, CatalogBrand.cs, and CatalogType.cs. EF6 maps catalog items to Catalog, brands to CatalogBrand, and types to CatalogType; each item requires one brand and one type.

Caching Strategy

No dedicated cache provider or cache policy was found. With UseMockData=true, Autofac registers CatalogServiceMock as a singleton containing a mutable in-memory list. The database-backed service uses EF6 and does not declare a query cache. ASP.NET session state is configured in-process but is not used as a catalog cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The application is a single bounded context and uses one catalog database; no cross-service database access or service-to-service data exchange was identified. The catalog service is the single application-level data access path, although it uses the EF DbContext directly rather than a separate repository abstraction.
